Hand-curated from the help article (not an automated collector).

P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: No restrictions in practice. Armenia has a liberal FX regime: residents and foreigners can hold foreign-currency accounts and import, export and exchange foreign currency relatively freely, under Central Bank of Armenia regulations and the Law on Currency Control.

L1_registration.answer: Freelancers register as an Individual Entrepreneur (Անհատ ձեռնարկատեր, IE) with the State Register. Both Armenian citizens and foreign nationals can register, often within a day. Fees were not captured.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by Armenia to the OECD: "Taxpayer Identification Number in Armenia is issued both to Entities and Individuals by State Register, where all business subjects must be registered. Only exception is for issuing TIN to the Commercial Banks. In this case TIN is issued by Central Bank. In all cases the structure of TIN is the same. Issued TIN should be used for all types of taxes, for all types of payments and tax returns." How a freelancer applies (forms, online portal, fees) was not captured.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents are taxed on worldwide income at a flat 20% unified income tax, with royalties at 10%. Small businesses, including individual entrepreneurs, can use turnover tax, which replaces CIT/PIT on business income and VAT, if prior-year income is under AMD 115 million; the rate depends on income type (not captured). Micro-entrepreneurship, for turnover up to AMD 24 million, gives exemption from several taxes subject to activity restrictions.

sources.title: Armenia - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 20%. Exported goods and services are generally zero-rated. Advertising, consulting, marketing, design, engineering, legal, accounting, audit, data-processing and related services are zero-rated where the recipient is outside Armenia. Turnover-tax payers (prior-year income under AMD 115 million) are outside VAT. Kintsugi (2026): a business becomes VAT-liable once turnover exceeds AMD 115 million; non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Armenian consumers must register regardless of turnover.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
